rules.description: HCPs must provide explicit, informed consent before any marketing communication. Silence or pre-ticked boxes do not constitute consent.
rules.implementation: Consent Management must be configured as opt-in by default. No communication channels enabled without explicit consent record.
rules.penalty: Up to 4% of annual global turnover or €20 million, whichever is higher

rules.description: HCPs can request deletion of all personal data. Must be actioned within 30 days.
rules.implementation: Data deletion workflow must cascade across all modules: Account, Visit History, Sample Transaction History, Email History, Consent Records. Anonymization is acceptable alternative for regulatory-required records (e.g., sample audit trails).

rules.description: HCPs can request their data in a machine-readable format.
rules.implementation: Export capability must cover: personal data, consent history, interaction history. Format: CSV or JSON. Response time: 30 days.

rules.description: Each data processing activity must have a documented lawful basis (consent, legitimate interest, legal obligation, etc.).
rules.implementation: Custom field or metadata on each module to record lawful basis. Consent module tracks consent-based processing; separate documentation for legitimate interest processing.

rules.description: Maintain records of all processing activities (Article 30).
rules.implementation: Enable Field Audit Trail for all modules processing personal data. Retain audit logs for minimum 5 years.

additional_rules: Bundesdatenschutzgesetz (BDSG) supplements GDPR with stricter employee data processing rules and a lower DPO threshold (20+ persons regularly processing personal data)
Works council (Betriebsrat) may need to approve CRM systems that track rep activity — start this approval process early as it can delay deployment by months
Stricter interpretation of legitimate interest — default to explicit opt-in consent for all HCP marketing communications
HWG (Heilmittelwerbegesetz) pharmaceutical advertising law requires mandatory content elements (Pflichtangaben) on every promotional material distributed via Field Email or Content Management
FSA Transparency Code requires annual disclosure of all transfers of value to HCPs/HCOs — Events Management must capture sufficient detail for FSA reporting
Sample limits are stricter than most EU countries: one smallest package per product per HCP per visit, maximum two per product per year
country_specific.see_also: germany-bdsg.json for comprehensive Germany-specific pharmaceutical rules

additional_rules: CNIL requires specific cookie consent mechanisms — banner must allow granular per-purpose acceptance/rejection
Transparency Code (Loi Bertrand / Sunshine Act) requires public disclosure of all HCP/HCO payments above EUR 10 — integrated with the Base Transparence Santé database
Anti-gift law (Loi anti-cadeaux) restricts hospitality, gifts, and benefits to HCPs — Events Management must enforce strict value caps and purpose documentation
ANSM (Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament) requires sample distribution reporting and imposes category-specific restrictions on sample quantities
French pharma industry code (LEEM) adds self-regulatory requirements on top of statutory rules
Garante per la protezione dei dati personali enforces additional marketing consent requirements — separate consent needed per channel (email, phone, SMS)
AIFA (Agenzia Italiana del Farmaco) regulations require specific visit logging fields for pharmaceutical rep interactions
Farmindustria transparency code requires disclosure of HCP transfers of value — CRM must track amounts in EUR with AIFA-compatible categories
Sample distribution is regulated by AIFA with per-product annual limits and mandatory request documentation from HCPs
AEMPS (Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios) regulates pharmaceutical promotion — promotional materials restricted to products marketed within the last 2 years
Farmaindustria self-regulatory code requires HCP payment transparency reporting
Regional (Comunidad Autónoma) variations exist for healthcare regulation — some regions have additional pharmaceutical rep registration requirements
Sample distribution limited to products with authorized promotional materials currently in force

migration_notes: When migrating from any source platform to target: (1) Consent records MUST be migrated with original consent dates, (2) Opt-out records are as important as opt-in records, (3) Consent granularity must match or exceed source platform (cannot consolidate separate channel consents into a single record), (4) Document the migration as a data processing activity in your Article 30 records.
